title: Not Very Effective
body: Frankly unimpressed. Before getting these, I used a bowl with a TBS of sugar, half a cup of warm water and a few tablespoons of apple cider vinegar with a few drops of Dawn. I also have three Zevo insect traps (basically very sticky plastic inside a plug in that has a warm blue light). The bowl traps were far more effective at getting a dozen of the buggers trapped (fruit fly invasion, and I do mean invasion). The "bait" in these apple traps obviously contains apple cider vinegar. But the flys would crawl around on the outside and only a few would actually end up in the trap. These traps are very small, and supposedly last 45 days which is ridiculous. After only a few days, they stopped working completely. The Zevo traps, on the other hand, had well over a hundred flies trapped. I had to change those traps out twice a week (it's normally like a month or two before they have to be changed, but INVASION of fruit flies). They are much more effective.

I opened them both at the same time and put them out. Immediately fruit flies started collecting around the rim of both containers but none seemed to want to go inside. I looked back at some of the reviews and found one person had used these in combination with a yellow sticky card and said it was very successful. title: Works but shouldn't be your only method
body: I had a bad infestation of fruit flies, worse then I have ever experienced this year. Fruit flies can come into your house on produce or they can develop in your drains. The product does work but if you have an infestation of fruit flies you must use several methods to exterminate them which takes time and patience.1. Throw ALL food you keep on your counters. This not only includes fruit but any other food you keep out. Fruit flies are attracted to fermenting foods. I had a mesh bag full of onions in my lazy Susan that I had to throw out because I found the flies in the bag.2. Deep clean your entire kitchen. The fuit flies continue the reproduce because they are laying their eggs on surfaces that are dirty. They can lay up to 500 eggs a day so if the adults keep having places to land aka fruit and sticky surfaces they will continue to reproduce. This means taking out everything on your counter and spraying with a cleaner solution.3. Last but not least, you need to find the source! Fruit flies can breed in your kitchen drain. This means using a solution to pour down the drain to kill the flies and eggs. There is solutions sold on Amazon that can be used. This needs several treatments and ensure your sink is always clean.In conclusion, you can get ride of fruit flies but it takes time. For me it took about 2 weeks. If you only use this trap, its just catching the flies but they will still reproduce if you don't give them a place to breed. Along with these traps, I made my own with apple cider vinegar. I deep cleaned my kitchen and bought the solution used to treat the sink for flies. One you kill the breeding ground, you just continue to set traps until the last adults are gone.Good Luck!

title: Amazingly effective!
body: We've been having a serious fruit fly/gnat infestation for years, and I'm almost positive they're breeding somewhere in our walls, floors or ceilings -- we've had leaks in the past, and I think we still do. So while it may take more than a trap to eradicate the gnat population here, this trap has brought us substantial relief, in just the span of 2-3 days.We can't call in the professionals at this point, for reasons I can't go into, but since the weather got warmer this spring, life in our small apartment was becoming unbearable. They were flying into our faces, landing on us, and landing in or on our food, even as we prepared it or ate it.I don't think it's been more than 48 hours, and there are A LOT of dead flies in the trap.We've caught substantial numbers with both homemade vinegar traps and the electronic Katchees, but this trap seems to summon the gnats, even from other rooms of the apartment (the trap is in the bedroom, but we also have a combination kitchen/LR, a bathroom and a foyer).Be warned, the trap does have a strict vinegar smell that wafts around, but the smell is NOTHING in comparison to the nuisance of the gnats.They do hang around the rim of the trap for a while, but then they definitely fly into it and die. We put it in an awkward place, and I don't want to take the chance of spilling it, so I can't get anything close to a count, but not only can I glimpse a large quantity of dead gnats, but I haven't seen ANY flying or landing anywhere else in our place, in many hours. This is truly amazing.I don't expect that it will eradicate them completely, because we don't know the breeding source, but one can always hope that all breeding adults will eventually fly around and find this thing. Until then, we may have to keep replacing the traps and finding ways to stretch out the liquid. Maybe we'll post an update, at some point.Meanwhile, I THANK GOD for the blessing of having this trap to control the terrible nuisance that was making our lives so unpleasant and difficult.Posting this update about 2-3 weeks later -- unfortunately in the warm weather (and we don't have air conditioning), these gnats are multiplying faster than the trap can catch them. Without it, we'd probably be swamped in gnats, fruit flies and whatever all these pests are. We'll have to put more traps around.

title: Not one fly: STEM Fruit Fly Trap
body: Followed the directions exactly. Left in the window where flies tend to congregate near plants and sun. Smells like vinegar. Did not catch one fly after two weeks. Moved to another location -- still no results.

title: Works but so does Apple Cider Vinager
body: Too expensivet. The cap is not the best for containing the bugs.

title: Make your own in description! No need to waste $$$
body: These traps don't last as long as they say, but don't worry! I bought a gallon of apple cider vinegar and a big bottle of unscented dish soap to make my own refills! And you can too! If you have a fruit fly problem, these are really just containers for the solution. I do love terro brand to an extent, but selling for this price for plastic, apple cider vinegar, and unscented dish soap is clownin.

title: A complete waste of your money!
body: We bought a bunch of these traps for our kitchen and bathroom and they do not seem to work at all. Don't waste your money. Better off with vineagar-soap solution in bowl with covering.

title: Does not word a waste of money

title: Inconvenient packaging and mediocre results
body: It catches enough flies (I guess?) but honestly like others are saying - you may as well have a home remedy if you’re just going to have an open jar of vinegar around. Also, one small movement and the entire bottle can be emptied since there is absolutely no form of filter/screen etc. on the top. Not a total waste of money but other products or a home remedy work better in my opinion.

title: Weak/Useless.
body: Return window closed when I learned these had failed. Better luck with a different brand.

title: Ineffective Product
body: This product did NOT work. I never felt so compelled to write reviews before and it’s not even too expensive in my opinion (though I do plan on pursuing a refund because of how useless it is.) I felt so frustrated with the problem of fruit flies suddenly appearing in my apartment for the first time ever. I was looking forward for this to do the trick. It didn’t. The flies were definitely attracted to the smell of the apple cider vinegar solution. They would sit on TOP of the apple but not go inside. Not a single one got trapped. I felt SO let down. I felt my Zevo plug-in to be more effective at luring fruit flies in. Albeit it is taking longer than expected. With the average lifespan of a fruit fly being 40-50 days, I hate the fact that I might need to wait 30 more days for all of them to die. I just don’t want to keep being let down by products as this one has. Super bummed.

title: Super Ninja Fruit Fly Traps: bait useless for my fruit flies while Terro brand bait has worked well.
body: I tried 3 different brands of liquid fruit fly attractant: in this home for 25 yrs but had never had a fruit fly problem in my life, they must have come in w/fruit which we don't buy a lot of: found out one female lays 500 eggs...This product, Super Ninja Fruit fly traps- I put several of these pre-filled bottles out for days but SUPER NINJA FRUIT FLY TRAPS DID NOT CATCH A SINGLE FRUIT FLY, compared to Terro brand used in the red plastic tomatoes, which worked well. I even tried the Super Ninja bait in the red Terro plastic tomatoe containers as some ads claimed the color + shape of the vessel played a role in attracting bugs but still no luck. The excellent Terro brand even worked well in a clear glass baby food jar. Terro works well, I see several of the fruit flies in the liquid. However, the tomatoe shaped plastic holders can tip easy, its a sticky, stinky liquid for which the company in South America would not tell me if it has a percent of poison in it- many of their products do, + they only give the number of poison control, + insist that the formula is 'proprietary information'. But after trying 3 brands, will stick w/Terro even though it does not sell a large container of liquid (I do not need more plastic tomatoe holders plus glass baby food jars worked just as well) Have put the Terro liquid bait-filled plastic tomatoes in clear plastic cups (clear so insects could see the red fruit shape), as the tomatoes have many preferations, which is good, but they are light-weight, tip + spill easily. However, the flat rectangular shape of the bottles of the Super Ninja Fruit fly Traps, though the liquid they came with is useless, the bottles w/their flat walls can be attached to any flat surface or wall w/a sticky strip; That had been my intent when I ordered them so I did not have to worry about containers spilling or space to put them down in or my cat getting to one... As the Ninja contents have proved useless, I will empty + rinse them out so I can fill them w/Terro attractant. will report if the insects will use these glass containers. While I had planned to take advantage of the flat walls of the Ninja glass containers + a photo in the Ad may have suggested they could be stuck to a wall, I was surprised that they came w/a pre-attached silicone sticky strip pre-attached for that purpose (one should use a spatula to remove the sticky strip and bottle intact from the wall (they are silicone w/adhesive + residue can be easily removed). There was one other brand of 25 vials which also did not catch a single fruit fly- even when used in Terro's tomatoe shape, which I also do not recommend, 'Qualirey 20 Pack Fruit Fly Trap Refill Liquid'... Do not recommend the Super Ninja Fly Traps because the bait does not work, at least for my fruit flies in Connecticut; but I still need to substitute Terro liquid bait in their their rectangular glass containers a+ see if the insects will then use them before I formally recommend the containers themselves- they have a yellow funnel on top. However, $39.99 plus tax is a high price to pay for the 12 glass containers which I will need to empty out to use with Terro brand liquid- if the bugs will use that container w/Terro bait.

title: not as described and ineffective
body: worthless. save your money. 1. The liguid solution that's supposed to last 180 days is not resealable, but is a twist off cap top. Once the cap top is removed there is no way to reseal it. 2. the product doesn't work. Caught no flies in 48 hours even though I deployed it in 4 locations in my house 3. Product is not eligible for returns Buy at electric fly zapper instead. They work great

title: Does not work at all!
body: We had a lot of fruit flies upon returning from vacation. We tried these traps and caught only two flies with them in two weeks! The jars do not have any way to trap the flies, the lid is wide open, and this is a flaw of design. If the lid had smaller holes in it, the flies would get trapped in there. The flies fly into these traps and do not stay there--whatever is in it does not attract or kill them. We got rid of our fruit flies using yellow sticky glue traps and other liquid fruit fly traps that have a better attractant and design to keep the flies trapped. And also good old-fashioned home-made vinegar, water, dish soap traps helped--with a dash of apple-cider vinegar as attractant or small piece of fruit in it.

title: Doesn’t kill them
body: Definitely attracts the fruit flies however they don’t go into trap there doesn’t kill them. I had better results just putting vinger in a bowl.

title: Barely works.
body: I’ve used other fly traps in the past in the same room where I set this one up at. They normally catch about 15-20 for a month, whereas this one only successfully caught 1 foolish gnat. Stinks up the room worse than others and also looks ugly and out of place. It’s easy to use, just unscrew the lid however. Just didn’t work and stunk badly. Just use apple cider vinegar and dish soap next time.
